topic_title.en: Introduction to Trigonometry — Quick Study Notes

detailed_explanation.en: This chapter's study points are organised below. Review each point and use the revision tips for quick recall.

en: Ratios are defined for acute angles in a right triangle
sin and cos of an angle never exceed 1
Key formulas and relations:
sin: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse
cos: cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse
tan: tan A = opposite/adjacent = sin A/cos A
Identity 1: sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1
Identity 2: 1 + tan^2 A = sec^2 A
Identity 3: 1 + cot^2 A = cosec^2 A
Complementary: sin(90-A) = cos A, tan(90-A) = cot A

revision_notes.en: Values for 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 deg: sin = 0, 1/2, 1/sqrt2, sqrt3/2, 1 | cos values are sin values in reverse order

summary.en: CSA = curved surface area, TSA = total surface area For combined solids, add volumes; do not add hidden joined faces

topic_title.en: Surface Areas and Volumes — Quick Study Notes

detailed_explanation.en: This chapter's study points are organised below. Review each point and use the revision tips for quick recall.

en: CSA = curved surface area, TSA = total surface area
For combined solids, add volumes; do not add hidden joined faces
Key formulas and relations:
Cylinder CSA: 2 pi r h
Cylinder TSA: 2 pi r (r + h)
Cylinder volume: pi r^2 h
Cone slant height: l = sqrt(r^2 + h^2)
Cone CSA: pi r l
Cone TSA: pi r (r + l)
Cone volume: 1/3 pi r^2 h
Sphere surface area: 4 pi r^2
Sphere volume: 4/3 pi r^3
Hemisphere CSA: 2 pi r^2
Hemisphere TSA: 3 pi r^2
Hemisphere volume: 2/3 pi r^3

revision_notes.en: When a solid is melted and recast, volume stays the same

topic_title.en: Statistics — Quick Study Notes

detailed_explanation.en: This chapter's study points are organised below. Review each point and use the revision tips for quick recall.

en: Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency
Mode is the most frequent value; modal class has highest frequency
Key formulas and relations:
Mean (direct): x_bar = sum(fx) / sum(f)
Mean (assumed mean): x_bar = a + sum(fd) / sum(f)

Mode: l + ((f1 - f0)/(2f1 - f0 - f2)) x h
Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean

summary.en: Always balance a chemical equation (mass is conserved) Combination: A + B -> AB

topic_title.en: Chemical Reactions and Equations — Quick Study Notes

detailed_explanation.en: This chapter's study points are organised below. Review each point and use the revision tips for quick recall.

en: Section: Chemistry
Always balance a chemical equation (mass is conserved)
Combination: A + B -> AB
Decomposition: AB -> A + B (heat, light or electricity)
Displacement: a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one
Double displacement: exchange of ions, often gives a precipitate
Oxidation = gain of oxygen or loss of electrons; reduction is the opposite
Corrosion (rusting) and rancidity are oxidation in daily life
Key formulas and relations:
Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2
Quicklime with water: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + heat
Electrolysis of water: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2

revision_notes.en: Endothermic absorbs heat, exothermic releases heat

topic_title.en: Light - Reflection and Refraction — Quick Study Notes

detailed_explanation.en: This chapter's study points are organised below. Review each point and use the revision tips for quick recall.

en: Section: Physics
Laws of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection
Concave mirror converges light; convex mirror diverges light
Convex lens converges; concave lens diverges
Convex mirror always gives a virtual, erect, diminished image
Sign convention: distances measured from pole in direction of incident light are positive
Light bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium
Key formulas and relations:
Focal length of mirror: f = R/2
Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f
Lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f
Magnification (mirror): m = h2/h1 = -v/u
Magnification (lens): m = h2/h1 = v/u
Snell's law: sin i / sin r = constant
Refractive index: n = c / v
Power of lens: P = 1/f (f in metres), unit dioptre

revision_notes.en: Concave mirror used in headlights and shaving mirrors; convex in rear-view mirrors

topic_title.en: Science — Quick Revision — Quick Study Notes

detailed_explanation.en: This chapter's study points are organised below. Review each point and use the revision tips for quick recall.

en: Matter exists as solid, liquid and gas
Atom is the smallest particle of an element; molecule is a group of atoms
Newton's laws: inertia, F = ma, action and reaction
Gravity pulls objects towards the Earth; g = 9.8 m/s^2
Work is done when force moves an object
Key formulas and relations:
Velocity: v = u + at
Distance: s = ut + 1/2 at^2
Third equation: v^2 = u^2 + 2as
Force: F = m x a
Work: W = F x s
Kinetic energy: KE = 1/2 m v^2
Potential energy: PE = m g h
Density: Mass / Volume
